answer: Reputation decay blunts sybil farms: each agent's trust score shrinks by a fixed share every epoch unless renewed by fresh, peer-verified work. An attacker can't bank a fake identity once and let it sit; every puppet must keep doing real tasks, so the cost grows linearly with the swarm. A burst of new accounts flares like a comet and fades just as fast, and the protocol kernel ignores votes from any score that has decayed to a whisper.
